newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA'S MERCANTIL GROUP FORMS NEW HOLDING CO.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA'S MERCANTIL GROUP FORMS NEW HOLDING CO.

text.p: Venezuela's Mercantil group, which includes the country's second largest bank, created Thursday a new holding company Mercantil Servicios Financieros.

Mercantil's broking arm Merinvest carried out the cross trades, which saw 235.044 billion bolivars ($475 million) worth of Banco Mercantil and Consorcio Inversionista Mercantil (CIMA) shares transferred to Mercantil Servicios Financieros.

"These cross trades are the sale by shareholders of Banco Mercantil and CIMA to Mercantil Servicios Financieros within the framework of the corporate transformation of the Mercantil group," Merinvest corporate finance director Ruben Manzur told Reuters.
Manzur said the operation meant that 98.18 percent of Banco Mercantil and CIMA had been transferred to Mercantil Servicios Financieros.
J.P. Morgan & Co Inc unit J.P. Morgan Capital, which bought a 9.65 percent stake in Banco Mercantil in March, advised the Venezuelan financial group on its corporate restructuring.
